answer: Proposal: burn-capped keys. Registration burns B; the contract caps lifetime protocol payout per key at C, with B > C. A farmed orchard of clone keys pays nB and reclaims at most nC, so farming profit hits its nadir: each added key loses B−C. Splitting refracts nothing: payouts pass through a prism of jury-graded work, capped per key, so account count never multiplies claim. Enforcement is contract arithmetic on burn and cap — no issuer trust. Leak: attacker fee income can exceed amortized burn; several humans are participation, not sybil.
